builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
summary: WISD replaces self-distillation methods that require privileged information or external teachers by training the model to minimize divergence from a weakened copy of itself created via low-bit quantization or magnitude pruning, using only unlabeled prompts. The cost is doubled memory during training (hosting both original and weakened models) plus computational overhead for the contrastive loss, though the weakened copy can reuse quantized weights efficiently. Post-adoption risks include divergence from the original model’s distribution leading to catastrophic forgetting, and sensitivity to the degradation level—if the weakened model is too corrupted, the contrast signal becomes noisy and training destabilizes.
rationale: The method requires only unlabeled prompts and commodity hardware, fitting constrained infrastructure, but the significant computational overhead and risk of instability necessitate workload-specific validation before full production adoption.

claims.statement: WISD replaces self-distillation methods that require privileged information or external teachers by training the model to minimize divergence from a weakened copy of itself created via low-bit quantization or magnitude pruning, using only unlabeled prompts. The cost is doubled memory during training (hosting both original and weakened models) plus computational overhead for the contrastive loss, though the weakened copy can reuse quantized weights efficiently. Post-adoption risks include divergence from the original model’s distribution leading to catastrophic forgetting, and sensitivity to the degradation level—if the weakened model is too corrupted, the contrast signal becomes noisy and training destabilizes.

Pruning and quantization variants improve average accuracy by 5.5 and 4.0 points respectively; Qwen3.5-4B gains 12.8 points on HMMT 2025 (57.7% to 70.5%) and 17.6 points on LiveCodeBench v6 (39.1% to 56.7%).
